label: conj:magic-numbers-from-q
title: Some functional of the Wedderburn-weighted Hoefsmit character data at $q_0$ carries nuclear shell structure
html:
The Wedderburn-weighted nuclear character signal \delta^2\Phi(Z), computed purely from the substrate parameter q_0 (per-partition Hoefsmit characters at Hecke levels k = 3\ldots 10, with no empirical input), is conjectured to carry nuclear shell structure.

For each partition \lambda \vdash k with Wedderburn weight w_\lambda = \dim_q(\lambda)^2/[k]_q!, the nuclear braid \mathcal{N}(Z, Z) has character \chi_\lambda(Z) computed from the Hoefsmit seminormal matrices. The cumulative Wedderburn-weighted signal

  \Phi(Z) = \sum_{k=3}^{K} \sum_{\lambda \vdash k} w_\lambda \, \ln|\chi_\lambda(Z)|

has forward second difference \delta^2 \Phi(Z) = \Phi(Z) - 2\Phi(Z{-}1) + \Phi(Z{-}2), which at K = 10 and q_0 takes the values

Z \delta^2 \Phi (K{=}10) Magic?
8 +33.25 \star
20 +20.40 \star
28 +4.43 \star

These three values are reproducible from q_0 with no empirical input. What they do not establish is any relation between \delta^2\Phi and the magic numbers; see the scope below.

Scope — this is a conjecture, and the tabulated values above are not evidence for it. Three measured facts bound what the signal can support. Each was obtained by re-running the producer over the full range Z \le 32, not by inspecting the three magic Z alone.

First, the sign of \delta^2\Phi is a parity test. Over Z = 3 \ldots 31 at K = 10, \delta^2\Phi(Z) > 0 holds precisely when Z is even, with no exceptions. Every magic number is even, so the positivity property is satisfied by every even Z and distinguishes none of them.

Second, the magic numbers are not maxima. Among even Z at K = 10 the local maxima are Z \in \{4, 12, 16\} — none magic — and the global maximum is Z = 12. The magic Z = 8 ranks sixth of the fourteen even Z in range, below the non-magic Z = 10 and Z = 12. The earlier reading of the table above as showing elevation at the magic numbers came from tabulating only magic Z; the non-magic contrast reverses it.

Third, no value of q repairs this. Sweeping q across 1 < q < \varphi (49 points, K = 8) moves the peak monotonically downward through Z — the global maximum runs 12 \to 16 \to 14 \to 12 \to 10 \to 8 as q rises — so the signal is genuinely q-dependent. But Z = 20 and Z = 2 are local maxima at no sampled q, and the best overlap with the magic set anywhere in the interval is two of four maxima. The parity property itself holds only for q \lesssim 1.16 and fails above.

What survives is the construction and its q-dependence, not the identification. Whether some other functional of the same Hoefsmit data carries shell structure is open; the second difference of the Wedderburn-weighted log-character, at any q in the interval tested, does not. The selection principle remains open at prop:homological-shell-condensation.
heading: Conjecture
